title: Gandharan Buddhist art
summary: Gandharan art, from what is now northern Pakistan and Afghanistan, can be traced to the 1st century BCE and flourished in the Kushan era, especially under King Kanishka in the 1st century CE. The life of the Buddha became its staple subject, with Buddha images in chapels, stupas and monasteries.

where.historical_name: Taxila, within Gandhara under the Kushan Empire

importance.justification: Gandharan sculpture is credited with early and abundant images of the Buddha and links Buddhist art to Silk Route exchange.

sources.title: Taxila Museum: a treasure trove of Gandhara civilisation
sources.author: Amjad Iqbal

reviewer_note: Gandhara spanned a wide area; the pin is Taxila, where the Dawn article places the museum collection from local sites. The start year is the 1st century BCE per World History Encyclopedia. Scholars differ on the peak, which these two pages do not settle.
